status: Authored by the Blindspot Lab team for the demonstration domain. Instructor-reviewable; not externally validated.
activation_rule: A concept is activated for a course only if at least two content units (or one heading) in that course contain one of its strong aliases.

topics.name: Measuring Marketing Performance
topics.description: Metrics that describe the scale and efficiency of marketing activity.

topics.name: Unit Economics
topics.description: How price, variable cost and volume combine into contribution and profit.

topics.name: Evidence and Decision-Making
topics.description: Judging evidence and making decisions when assumptions change.

concepts.name: Revenue and conversion metrics
concepts.description: Revenue is price multiplied by units sold; the conversion rate is conversions divided by visitors. Rates and absolute counts answer different questions, and percentage-point changes differ from percent changes.

concepts.name: Contribution margin
concepts.description: Contribution margin per unit is price minus variable cost per unit; total contribution covers fixed costs before becoming profit. Price changes alter contribution per unit by the full amount of the change.

concepts.name: Return on advertising spend (ROAS)
concepts.description: ROAS is attributed revenue divided by advertising spend. It is not a profit measure: the break-even ROAS equals 1 divided by the contribution margin ratio.

concepts.name: Customer acquisition cost and lifetime value
concepts.description: CAC is sales and marketing spend divided by new customers. CLV estimates contribution (not revenue) over the customer relationship; CLV-to-CAC and payback compare the two.

concepts.name: Correlation, causation and experiments
concepts.description: Correlation does not establish causation; confounders can create associations. Randomised experiments estimate causal effects, and statistical significance differs from practical significance.

concepts.name: Decisions under changing assumptions
concepts.description: Sensitivity and scenario analysis test how conclusions depend on assumptions; the median describes typical values in skewed data while the mean supports totals.
